candidates.name: Datum height differences
verified_facts: OS explains that differences between historic height datums such as Liverpool and Newlyn vary geographically because of historical levelling networks.
Ordnance Datum Newlyn is based on mean sea level at Newlyn and subsequent national precise levelling.
A single universal offset between historic datums is not valid across Great Britain.
semantic_limits: Historic datum comparisons are vertical-reference context only and cannot be applied as a universal correction to parcel LiDAR heights.

candidates.name: Search for passive stations
verified_facts: The legacy passive GPS network contains around 900 stations established for high-accuracy positioning before current OS Net use became standard.
OS publishes indicative standard errors for passive station coordinates, including plan and ellipsoidal-height uncertainty.
The passive-station information is part of OS legacy control data and is no longer maintained as the current national active network.
semantic_limits: Legacy passive-station coordinates and their published uncertainties cannot be treated as current parcel observations or as a replacement for OS Net/OSTN15/OSGM15 and source-specific raster evidence.
